desc:
The string s contains only the letters L and R, and it has the same number of each. A string is balanced if it has the same number of L and R.

Cut s into consecutive non-empty pieces so that every piece is balanced. Return the largest possible number of pieces.

s = "RLRRLLRLRL"  ->  4   ("RL" + "RRLL" + "RL" + "RL")
s = "LLLRRR"      ->  1
constraints: s has equally many L and R (so its length is even)
hints: A piece is balanced when its number of L equals its number of R. How can you track that while scanning from the left?
Keep a running balance: +1 for L, -1 for R. A piece can end exactly where the balance returns to zero.
Cut greedily at every position where the running balance is zero; cutting as early as possible can never reduce the number of pieces. Count those positions.
editorial: Give L the value +1 and R the value -1 and keep a prefix sum. Pieces s[a..b) are balanced exactly when the prefix sum at a equals the prefix sum at b. Starting from prefix 0 at the front and ending at prefix 0 (the whole string is balanced), a valid cutting is a chain of positions with prefix sum 0.

Using every position with prefix sum 0 as a cut gives the maximum number of pieces, since any valid cutting uses a subset of those positions and the pieces between consecutive zero positions are already balanced. So the answer is the number of times the running balance hits zero. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) space.
